lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Replace the contact URL if it is a placeholder.
items.because: It should lead directly to a working, professional profile.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They generally do not belong on a U.S. resume.

items.says: Include the education location only if it adds clarity.
items.because: The degree, school, and dates are sufficient.

items.says: Consider giving the Lakeside role less space for finance applications.
items.because: It should not displace stronger finance evidence.

items.says: Change the past-tense verb.
items.because: The Lakeside role is marked “Present.”

items.says: Check that five rounds a week reflects the current or typical workload.
Specify the responsibility or scale of the junior tournament.
items.because: “Helped” does not show what you contributed.

items.says: Clarify what the 40% efficiency improvement measures and how it was measured.
items.because: It could refer to time to close, hours worked, or another metric.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the modeling versus the shared template.
Make clear that the standardization result follows from what you did.
Explain whether the board-pack commentary informed decisions or follow-up.
items.because: The 5% threshold describes the process, not its impact.

items.says: Correct the acquisition-valuation methodology.
items.because: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC is inconsistent.

items.says: Recalculate the claimed group EBITDA margin.
items.because: Group EBITDA margin cannot be obtained by adding business-unit margins.

items.says: Explain how forecast error was measured.
Explain how the forecast enabled early debt repayment.
items.because: The forecast may have merely coincided with it.

items.says: Check whether the loan vintages support a first-two-years default claim.
items.because: Only loans with a full two years of observation can support it.

items.says: Clarify whether the default outcome covers all 60 loans or only approved loans.
Substantiate the claim of no rise in early defaults and give the comparison period.
items.because: Otherwise, the outcome may sound more conclusive than the data supports.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The Crescent role ended in 2022.

items.says: Confirm that the seven-to-one reduction compares like annual periods.
Clarify whether the time saving covers the whole credit memo or just financial spreading.
items.because: The claim should match what was measured.

items.says: Distinguish work still underway from the completed model and spring pitch.
items.because: The project is marked “Present.”

items.says: Emphasize the valuation process rather than proximity to market price.
items.because: The market price may have been visible while you built the model.

items.says: Identify which discount-rate change produced the value change.
Remove or verify the FP&A-support claim.
items.because: FP&A support seems out of place in an investment-fund role.

items.says: Make the FP&A description more specific.
items.because: It is too broad to assess.

items.says: Clarify what changed in the committee’s use of the report, if substantiated.
Remove the cash-forecast bullet unless it was genuinely a separate project.
items.because: It closely duplicates the Stonebridge claim, including the business size, forecast error, and debt repayment.

items.says: The cash-forecast claim conflicts with the fund’s 2018–19 dates.
List only tools you can use at the level a hiring team would expect.
Avoid padding the methods list.
items.because: The project and experience bullets already provide evidence for several listed methods.
